mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a concussion and a TBI?

acceptedAnswer.text: A concussion is a mild form of traumatic brain injury (TBI) caused by a bump, blow, or jolt to the head that causes the brain to move rapidly inside the skull. While concussions are generally considered less severe, they are still TBIs. A TBI is a broader term encompassing any injury to the brain resulting from an external force, ranging from mild concussions to severe, life-threatening brain damage. All concussions are TBIs, but not all TBIs are concussions.
acceptedAnswer.description: A concussion is a mild form of traumatic brain injury (TBI); TBI is a broader term for any brain injury from an external force, making all concussions a type of TBI.
